purpose: Every finding from the unsolved.md work, written at the moment it lands, so an agent that runs out of usage mid-task loses nothing. Append-only. Read this file FIRST on resume.

schema.at: ISO 8601 local time the finding was made
schema.by: agent that made it (fable-5.2, deepseek-v4.1-flash, argon, human)
schema.item: the construct or task, one line
schema.finding: what is actually true, in plain words
schema.evidence: reproduction path and the numbers that prove it

resume.build: export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH; cd /tmp/rg-fable-wt && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rg-fable-target cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --features "deep parser"
resume.tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rg-fable-test cargo test  (then again with --features "deep parser")
resume.rule: Write one entry here the moment a finding survives a reproduction. Do not batch them to the end of the run - the last run died mid-task and only the uncommitted diff survived.

entries.item: js corpus is a random sample of every .js under both home trees
entries.finding: A large share of the js corpus was built output - webpack chunks, .next/static, dist, .min.js. Each is one enormous line, so per-line pairing has nothing to compare and its losses are noise no reader fix can remove. That is why js had been stuck at a low file count with high losses.
entries.evidence: old sample /tmp/opencode/sweep-local/js-minified-baseline: 96/1995 files, 164 losses. New source-only sample: 149/2000 files, 270 losses - fewer files pass because they contain constructs. Filter: /tmp/opencode/js-source-filter.py (>=15 lines, no line >400 chars, built dirs excluded); sweep-local.sh pipes through it.

entries.item: class field with a computed key: `static [entityKind] = "x"`
entries.finding: The lexer named the target `static` because unpack_targets only stripped const/let/var/my/our/local/val/mut; a class-field modifier is not a binding. The CST names the computed key, which is right.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-static/a.js (4 lines): 1 loss -> 0. js 149/270 -> 138/244, ts 91/114 -> 84/107, python and rust held.

entries.item: rust method call after a block-like operand: `async { s }.boxed()`
entries.finding: After a block-like operand in statement position the grammar writes `.name(args)` as one field_expression carrying its own arguments, so no call_expression exists to read and the call left the record. Treating a field_expression with an arguments child as a call repairs it.
entries.evidence: src/deep_facts/rust.rs: rust_block_method + rust_call/rust_callee. Measured by deepseek-v4.1-flash in /tmp/rg-fable-wt: rust 260/1816 (287) -> 255/1816 (282); js, ts, python untouched.

entries.item: js for-header assignment emits an event the CST does not have
entries.finding: For `for (i = length; i-- !== 0;)` the lexer emits an `a` event with targets [i]; the CST emits nothing on that line because it records a for header's binder in the statement's target list. Suspect double accounting on the lexer side, but not yet confirmed against pipeline.rs.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-for/a.js reproduces 2 losses (lines 17 and 32); the corpus shows 11 rows, but only about 2 distinct files.

entries.item: corpus duplication inflates every corpus, worst in rust
entries.finding: Measured by content hash: js 2000 files / 1854 unique (7% dup), ts 2000 / 1537 (23%), rust 1816 / 1000 (45%). The rust corpus is every .rs in the workspace, which now holds many near-identical worktrees, so almost half the rust losses are the same code counted again. Dedupe would reset every rust baseline - owner decision, not a lane decision.

entries.item: usage limit stopped the run mid-task
entries.finding: Fable 5.2 hit its 5-hour limit at 12:36 EST, resets 17:10 (America/New_York). It had applied the rust field_expression fix but not committed it. Its measurement helpers and reproductions are in /tmp/fable-m/tools and /tmp/fable-r.
